a_meteor_3dep_1m.dataset: USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar DTM, tile USGS_1M_12_x49y388_AZ_NorthEast_D23
a_meteor_3dep_1m.read: windowed /vsicurl/ read of a 3.6 x 3.6 km window (no full download), 3600 x 3600 px

methods.centre: Iterative: 72 azimuth sectors of 5 deg; in each, the radius of the highest sector-mean elevation within 0.6-1.5x the current rim radius is the rim-crest point; a least-squares (Kasa) circle is fit to those points; repeated 5 times from the first guess.
methods.profile: Azimuthally averaged radial profile: mean elevation of all valid pixels in rings of width dr (dr = pixel size, 2 m for 1 m data) around the fitted centre; pixel distances in metres in a projected CRS.
methods.rim_crest_diameter_m: 2 x the radius of the maximum of the radial mean profile (searched 0.5-1.6x the fitted circle radius).
methods.rim_crest_diameter_azimuthal_m: 2 x mean of the 72 per-sector rim-crest radii (spread given as std).
methods.depth_m: Profile maximum (mean rim crest) minus profile minimum inside 0.5 x rim radius (mean floor).
methods.rim_height_m: Profile maximum minus the median of all pixels at 2.2-2.8 x rim radius (surrounding plain/ejecta apron).
methods.max_wall_slope_profile_deg: Steepest inner-wall slope of the radial mean profile: max atan(dz/dr) over r < rim radius, dz/dr by central differences over a 2 x dr baseline.
methods.wall_slope_pixel_p95_deg: 95th percentile of per-pixel slope (central-difference gradient, 2-pixel baseline) for pixels on the inner wall, 0.3-0.95 x rim radius. Shows local steepness the averaged profile hides.

note: All numbers come from runs of lidar/crater_profiles.py. Profiles are stored in data/raw/lidar/profiles.json, not here. Written with SI assistance (Claude Code).

b_meteor_glo30.crs: EPSG:4326 lon/lat, heights EGM2008; pixel centres transformed to EPSG:26912 for distances

lidar30_vs_glo30.offset_note: GLO-30 heights are EGM2008, 3DEP NAVD88, so a constant offset is expected; RMS values are after removing it.
lidar30_vs_glo30.method: 1 m lidar averaged in 30 x 30 m blocks; GLO-30 sampled bilinearly at block centres after an exact lon/lat -> UTM 12N transform of every GLO-30 pixel centre (no resampling of GLO-30 for the measurements).

c_moon_lola_20m.dataset: LOLA south-pole DEM LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ (PGDA product 90, Barker et al. 2023)
c_moon_lola_20m.crs: Moon south polar stereographic, R = 1737.4 km, metres; heights relative to 1737.4 km sphere
c_moon_lola_20m.selection: Automatic search of the cached 30 m copy (+-80 km around the pole): difference-of-Gaussians minima (sigma 6 and 25 px), each measured with the same profile method; kept 1000 <= D <= 1500 m; ranked by d/D - 0.5*(rim radius std / R) - 0.05*(rim elevation std / depth) - 0.004*(regional tilt deg). The winner was then re-read and re-measured at native 20 m.
c_moon_lola_20m.read: windowed /vsicurl/ read with retries, 187 x 187 px

d_morasko.dataset: GUGiK NMT 1 m DTM (ALS), WCS coverage DTM_PL-KRON86-NH_TIFF; Copernicus GLO-30 for comparison
d_morasko.crater_detection: difference-of-Gaussians minima (sigma 8 and 30 m) in the 1 m DTM, each measured with the same profile method as Meteor Crater from first-guess radii 15/25/40/60 m; kept if rim radius std / R <= 0.12, d/D >= 0.05, rim above the surroundings; the largest rim-crest diameter is reported

glo30_same_area.method: GLO-30 reprojected bilinearly onto a 30 m EPSG:2180 grid over the same 1 x 1 km box; closed-depression depth by sink filling (morphological reconstruction, box border as outlet).

d_morasko.caveat: Morasko is a counter-example, not a Moon analog: small craters in forest on glacial sediment; the largest may hold water, so its lidar floor is the water/ground surface at survey time.

c_wall_slope_at_similar_pixel_size.note: The steepest slope of an averaged profile falls with pixel size, so the lunar crater (20 m pixels) is to be compared with Meteor Crater at 30 m, not at 1 m. One crater on each body: an illustration, not a statistic.
